text:
maria: incoming from support — enterprise customer (acme-corp) reporting lots of 5xx / gateway timeouts hitting hosted inference since 09:12 UTC. They say errors started right after our staged rollout. request IDs: rqd_34a1, rqd_34b2, rqd_34c3. sample error: "502 Bad Gateway: upstream read timeout". Can oncall take? :rotating_light:

liam: i'm on it. pinging runtime + infra. maria, can you paste the exact curl they used and any headers (don’t paste full API key)?

maria: sent repro snippet from customer (redacted):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx...REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-13b-v2","input":"Summarize sales deck"}'
```

maria: they see 5xx ~40% of requests for a short window, latency spikes >10s, then some success. They attached a few kube-proxy/gateway traces.

deploy-bot: deploy event: user-triggered staged rollout v2026-03-17_09:10 -> route group alpha weight 20% -> featureflag:prefetch-window=true (by nia)

nia: i rolled the staged flag update at 09:09 for alpha slice. nothing else changed in infra.

raj: looking at runtime telemetry — fetch KV cache miss rate jumped when that flag flipped, batcher queue latencies increased, and nginx upstream timeouts spiked. seeing many downstream 502s from inference-workers returning EOF on stream.

liam: can you paste the relevant logs/snippets? even a few lines helps.

raj: logs (trimmed):

```
[09:12:15] inference-worker-23 | ERROR rpc: failed to stream tokens to client: write tcp 10.12.8.3:443->10.14.2.18:51234: write: connection reset by peer
[09:12:16] router | WARN upstream request timed out after 8s -> 502
[09:12:17] batcher | INFO batch size 1 latency 7800ms (prefetch disabled: false)
```

raj: hypothesis: the prefetch-window toggle changed batching behaviour for small requests, causing a combination of more small batches and increased concurrent connections, exposing a resource exhaustion issue in the worker pool.

sophia: Acme is on Dedicated contract — they flagged this as high priority and our CSM is getting escalations. they need ETA and a mitigation plan.

liam: action plan: 1) revert the staged flag for alpha -> set prefetched-window back to previous value 2) if that fails, short-term rollback of v2026-03-17_09:10 rollout to 0% 3) open follow-up to root cause. who can flip the flag now?

nia: i can flip the flag for alpha now. doing it.

nia: flipped prefetched-window=false for alpha at 09:18 UTC.

ops-bot: alert cleared? monitoring: 5xx rate dropped from 38% -> 6% in alpha within 120s of flag flip.

maria: acme confirms reduced errors and latency improving. they still saw a couple of timeouts but much better. :relieved:

liam: great. can we hold staged rollout paused and not continue until we have a postmortem? i've disabled further staged rollouts for that flag.

raj: capturing telemetry dump and will run a small repro with the prefetched-window=true config in our perf rig to reproduce resource exhaust. initial guess: worker kernel path + connection pooling + small-batch pathological case.

nia: i’ll also check kernel-selector heuristics on the alpha pool and any connection limits at the envoy/nginx layer.

maria: CSM notified. Acme asked for timeline for a permanent fix — can we give an ETA for investigation?

liam: we’ll do a triage doc in the incidents runbook. aim for triage complete in 2 hours and a follow-up postmortem within 48h.

sophia: i'll update the customer with that timeline and offer an interim support window.

raj: repro steps (internal): run the same small prompt load with model rwd-13b-v2, prefetched-window=true, concurrency ramp to 60 qps with high small-batch fraction. watch batcher queue latency and worker fd counts.

liam: thanks. next steps assigned: raj (runtime repro + logs), nia (infra config check + rollback safety), maria/sophia (customer comms), liam (postmortem owner). label this P0.

maria: adding incident tag and creating follow-up ticket INC-2026-1432. closing this thread for immediate ops — reopen if errors recur. :white_check_mark:
